title: Walking between
tomorrow: why did desert monks call the afternoon a demon?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the food arrived: Rabbi Levi's two psalms, the food God's before the blessing and given to you after. Lunch is over. Now the walk back to work.

The walk back from lunch usually happens on fast-forward: head down, already inside the next task, half-jogging to be on time. A companion of the Prophet named Abu Qatada remembers a day when some people ran. They were praying behind the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, when he heard a commotion: latecomers hurrying to catch up. When the prayer ended, he turned and asked what all that noise had been. We were rushing to the prayer, they said. Late, and eager to make it. His answer was about their feet.
screen: `LUNCH ON FAST-FORWARD.` → `LATECOMERS RUNNING TO PRAY.` → `WHAT WAS THAT NOISE?`

segments.voice: Don't do that, he told them. When you come to the prayer, come with calm. Pray what you catch with everyone, and complete what you missed. In another saying he puts it as a pair: walk to the prayer with calm and with dignity, and don't hurry. The Arabic word for that calm is sakina, a settled stillness, and in the Qur'an it's the name of a peace God sends down into believers' hearts. So the Prophet asked for that peace in the walking, not only in the prayer. Here is the teaching, named plainly. In Islam, the walk to prayer already belongs to the worship. Another hadith in Bukhari says that whoever washes for prayer and walks to the mosque for nothing but the prayer is raised a degree with each step, and a sin is taken away. The steps count. That's why the teaching is to walk to the mosque calmly, even when the prayer has already begun. Running would spend the walk to save a minute. Notice what the Prophet didn't say. He didn't say be late, or stay home. Getting there mattered. He said the in-between is part of where you're going, so walk it with calm. The Qur'an describes the servants of the Merciful as people who walk upon the earth gently, and answer the foolish with peace. On your own path, with the tag left on: the walk between two things isn't dead time to rush through. It's a short path of its own. Something to tell a friend tonight: told about people running late, the Prophet didn't say hurry. He said come with calm.
screen: `COME WITH CALM.` · `SAKINA: A PEACE SENT DOWN.` · `EVERY STEP IS COUNTED.` · `THE WALK BELONGS TO WHERE YOU'RE GOING.` · then, large: `BETWEEN.`

segments.voice: Stand and walk slowly across the room and back, a few steps each way, with the calm the Prophet asked for on the way to prayer. Feel each foot lift and land. If a rush rises in you, let the next step be a little slower than the last. At each end, pause, turn, and begin again.
Walking between: the walk from one thing to the next, done with calm. In Islam, the walk to prayer is part of the prayer, every step counted.
Carry this one: between, the walk from one thing to the next, done with calm, every step counted. Until tomorrow.
